questions.stem: 4.0 g of sodium hydroxide is dissolved in water and made up to 500 cm3 of solution. What is the concentration in mol/dm3? [Na = 23, O = 16, H = 1]
questions.explanation: The molar mass of NaOH is 40 g/mol, so 4.0 g is 4.0 / 40 = 0.10 mol. The volume is 500 / 1000 = 0.500 dm3. Concentration = 0.10 / 0.500 = 0.20 mol/dm3.

distractorRationale.a: The moles were divided by 2 instead of by 0.5, halving rather than doubling
distractorRationale.b: The volume was treated as 1 dm3, so the 500 cm3 conversion was skipped
distractorRationale.d: The mass in grams was divided by the volume in dm3 without converting to moles

questions.stem: A solution of sulphuric acid has a concentration of 0.50 mol/dm3. What is its concentration in g/dm3? [H = 1, S = 32, O = 16]
questions.explanation: The molar mass of H2SO4 is (2 x 1) + 32 + (4 x 16) = 98 g/mol. Multiplying the molar concentration by the molar mass gives 0.50 x 98 = 49 g/dm3.

distractorRationale.a: A concentration of 0.1 mol/dm3 was used instead of 0.5
distractorRationale.c: This is the concentration of a 1.0 mol/dm3 solution, so the 0.5 factor was omitted
distractorRationale.d: The molar mass was divided by 0.5 instead of multiplied

questions.stem: 25 cm3 of a 2.0 mol/dm3 hydrochloric acid solution is diluted with distilled water to a final volume of 250 cm3. The concentration of the diluted solution is
questions.explanation: Dilution does not change the moles of solute, so C1V1 = C2V2. Rearranging gives C2 = (2.0 x 25) / 250 = 50 / 250 = 0.20 mol/dm3. The volume increased tenfold, so the concentration fell to one tenth of its original value.

distractorRationale.a: The dilution factor was applied twice, dividing by 100 instead of 10
distractorRationale.c: A dilution factor of 4 was used instead of 10
distractorRationale.d: The formula was inverted, multiplying rather than dividing by the volume ratio

questions.stem: How many moles of solute are present in 20 cm3 of a 0.10 mol/dm3 solution?
questions.explanation: Number of moles = concentration x volume in dm3. Converting the volume gives 20 / 1000 = 0.020 dm3, so n = 0.10 x 0.020 = 0.0020 mol, which can also be written as 2.0 x 10^-3 mol.

distractorRationale.b: The volume in cm3 was divided by 1000 but the concentration factor was then omitted
distractorRationale.c: The volume was treated as 2 dm3 rather than 0.02 dm3
distractorRationale.d: The volume in cm3 was used directly without converting to dm3

questions.stem: What mass of potassium hydroxide, in grams, is required to prepare 250 cm3 of a 0.40 mol/dm3 solution? [K = 39, O = 16, H = 1]
questions.explanation: Moles needed = concentration x volume = 0.40 x (250 / 1000) = 0.40 x 0.250 = 0.10 mol. The molar mass of KOH is 39 + 16 + 1 = 56 g/mol, so the mass required is 0.10 x 56 = 5.6 g.

questions.stem: A molar solution is one that contains

options.text: one gram of solute per cubic decimetre of solution
one mole of solute per cubic decimetre of solution
one mole of solute per cubic decimetre of solvent
one mole of solute in any volume of solution

questions.explanation: A molar solution has a concentration of exactly 1 mol/dm3, meaning one mole of solute in every cubic decimetre of the final solution. The reference is always to the total volume of solution, not to the volume of water added.

distractorRationale.a: One gram per cubic decimetre is a mass concentration, not a molar one
distractorRationale.c: Volume of solvent and volume of solution are not the same, because dissolving changes the total volume
distractorRationale.d: Concentration must state a volume; one mole in an unspecified volume tells you nothing
